lesson.title: Read a title from JSON
lesson.summary: Write readTitle(text): return a record’s string title, or null for malformed JSON or the wrong data shape.
explanation: JSON stores data as text. Parsing converts that text into a JavaScript value.
Check the value before reading its fields. `typeof value === "object"` alone is not enough: null and arrays also have that typeof result.
The practice accepts a title even when it is an empty string. It rejects missing or numeric titles; it does not convert them into text.

`JSON.stringify` goes the other direction for ordinary JSON-compatible data.
```javascript
console.log(JSON.stringify({ city: "Oslo" }));
```
It returns JSON text. Not every JavaScript value can be preserved by JSON.
steps: Write readTitle(text): return a record’s string title, or null for malformed JSON or the wrong data shape.
Run the checks and inspect the result.
Change one input or rule and explain what changes.

quiz.question: JSON.parse('{"title":17}') succeeds. Your app needs a text title. What should readTitle return under this lesson’s contract?
choices: "17", because JSON converts every field to text
null, because the parsed title is not a string
quiz.explanation: Parsing verifies JSON syntax, not the app’s required record shape. The number 17 is valid JSON but fails the string-title requirement.

hints: Wrap parsing in try/catch so malformed text follows the failure path.
Reject null, arrays, and nonobjects before reading title.
Check typeof value.title rather than whether title is truthy; empty text is allowed.
